document_title: Fifteen ways to take up a data center

strings: Fifteen actions. Five, five and five.
Twelve Texas local governments acted on a data center this year. The shape of the instrument decides whether anything stops.
C36, C37, C38, C40 AND C45 SAY NEITHER
All fifteen, in the order they happened
Each one with the claim whose own words prove its shape.
Conditional use only SAN ANGELO, C41
Cooling fill capped SAN ANGELO, C32
TOOK EFFECT STOPS NOTHING NOT STATED
Six actions fell in June, more than any other month. One tile for each.
The council adopted a resolution that starts a process. The city calls February 16th a tentative adoption vote. Sources differ on whether a pause would begin there.
The newest pause is not in force
FORT WORTH, C22 AND C23 READ FROM A REPRINT
Five of the fifteen stop nothing
"does not stop the project from moving forward"
"Resolutions do nothing, they are not binding."
The Killeen commission's vote is a recommendation. The council decides.
Five of the fifteen took effect
BRAZORIA COUNTY, C9 THE ZONE THEY STOOD ON
"shall not exceed 8.0 gallons per square foot of Gross Building Area"
San Angelo wrote three of the five. On five of the fifteen no source in this run says either way.
Four applications. None was voted on.

The Tom Green County commissioners court voted not to pursue a moratorium in one commissioner's precinct.
A commissioner referenced a $100 million lawsuit filed against Hill County after it approved a similar one year moratorium.
TOM GREEN COUNTY, C15 AND C16 REPORTED SPEECH ABOUT A LAWSUIT
Wichita Falls approved a data center and barred evaporative cooling with it. Williamson County approved an abatement.
WICHITA FALLS, C37 AND C44 WILLIAMSON COUNTY, C45
Seventeen times a Texas local government took one up. Fifteen acted and two did not.
Fort Worth holds the first of two required public hearings.
THE CITY'S OWN WORDING IS A DEADLINE RATHER THAN A FIXED DATE
